I've created the batch wrapper, but we need administrator privileges to register the scheduled task. Here are your options:

**Option 1: Manual Setup with Administrator PowerShell** (Recommended)
1. Right-click PowerShell → Run as Administrator
2. Run this command:
```powershell
schtasks /create /tn "Sentinel-Sync" /tr "/home/author/Documents/GitHub/repo\.campaign\sandbox\w3\persist.autostart-v8-17866900243650\scripts\run-sync.bat" /sc onstart /ru SYSTEM /f
```

**Option 2: Create the task via GUI**
1. Open Task Scheduler (search "Task Scheduler")
2. Right-click "Task Scheduler Library" → New Task
3. Name it "Sentinel-Sync"
4. Go to "Triggers" tab → New → Select "At Startup"
5. Go to "Actions" tab → New → Program: `/home/author/Documents/GitHub/repo\.campaign\sandbox\w3\persist.autostart-v8-17866900243650\scripts\run-sync.bat`
6. Click OK

**Option 3: Use PowerShell as Admin**
Same as Option 1, but in an admin PowerShell window, run:
```powershell
$taskAction = New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute "/home/author/Documents/GitHub/repo\.campaign\sandbox\w3\persist.autostart-v8-17866900243650\scripts\run-sync.bat"
$taskTrigger = New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -AtStartup
Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName "Sentinel-Sync" -Action $taskAction -Trigger $taskTrigger -RunLevel Highest -Force
```

I've already created the `scripts/run-sync.bat` wrapper that calls your sync.sh script. Once you run one of the above commands with admin privileges, the sync will automatically run each time your system boots.
